 The Montana State University football team is back in action on Saturday in Greely, Colorado to take on Northern Colorado at 5 pm MT. 
 The game initially was scheduled for noon, before nationwide flight delays impacted the team.
 The Bears are 3-7 this season and 2-5 in Big Sky Conference Play.
 They have beaten Northeastern State (Division II), Utah Tech and Cal Poly. They have lost to Weber State, South Dakota, Wyoming (FBS), Montana, Eastern Washington, UC Davis and most recently Southern Utah.
 Northern Colorado is one of the better defenses in the conference, ranking No. 3 in total defense, No. 3 in scoring defense (allowing 26 points per game), No. 3 in rush defense (allowing 146 rush yards per game), No. 6 in pass defense (allowing 245 pass yards per game) and No. 7 in redzone defense.
 “They got a good front,” MSU head coach Brent Vigen said. “All these teams that are in that category of being in the upper, whatever third or whatever you want to say in defense, it starts with the guys up front. I do think they know what they want to do, and there's an aggressive nature to how they play. There are some, I suppose, similarities in their ability to want to move and twist up front. That's got to be well thought out, well coordinated. That makes it hard on a run game, so I think it's a combination of having good players, having a scheme they understand, and then they can go out and execute. Having a mindset as a football team that they want to be able to run it on offense and they want to be able to stop it on defense, I think is certainly at the core of who they are, and you can see that week in week out.”
 UNC’s leading tackler is junior linebacker Hudson Voggesser who has racked up 63 total tackles this season.
 Dominic Butts, a senior defensive lineman for the Bears, leads the team in sacks with 2.5 this season.
 Offensively, the Bears are No. 10 in total offense, No. 11 in scoring offense (22 points per game), No. 5 in rushing offense (176 rush yards per game), No. 12 in passing offense (205 pass yards per game) and No. 12 in redzone offense.
 The Bears have deployed numerous different quarterbacks this season, headlined by the four different signal-callers that took a snap in their game against Eastern Washington, but the team’s leading passer this season is senior Brayten Silbor.
 Silbor started at FCS powerhouse and prestigious university, Lehigh. Where he saw limited action in 2022, then he was named the full-time starter in 2023. He sat out the entire 2024 season due to injury, then went to Southwestern Community College in 2025. Finally, he landed at Northern Colorado this past summer and he has thrown for 972 yards, five touchdowns and three interceptions this season.
 “He's (Silbor) clearly in their eyes the best option,” Vigen said. “Meaning the best option probably to be this dual threat. To be able to throw it to the guys they have, which are a very capable group, and to be an athletic enough runner as well. And I know they, in this past game, they mixed in (Keegan) Patterson as well, at least a little bit. Anytime you're playing multiple guys, that's challenging. These are guys that in that room that have college experience. I know he's (Silbor) been three different places, I believe, and you know (he is) probably just to some degree even finding his footing in Greeley, but I think he's a very capable guy. Over the course of the season, he's done some really good things, and you know, like any week, the more uncomfortable we can make whoever's playing quarterback, we need to be able to do that with him.”
 Montana State is coming off an emotional triple-overtime win last Saturday in Pocatello over Idaho State, and they will face rival Montana next week at home for The Brawl, but they remain singularly focused on this week’s opponent, UNC.
 “Taco (Dowler) talked about that this morning briefly in the position room, those guys (Montana) got to focus on their game this week because they go play a team that we just played and they're not thinking about us for sure,” MSU junior wide receiver Dane Steel said. “If they (Montana) want any hopes of the playoffs, they're thinking about that week, or this week, sorry, and you know it's easy for us, (we) just got to focus on one game. Next week means nothing if we don't take care of business this week.”
 The Bobcats will look to improve to 10-1 this season on Saturday at 12pm MT against Northern Colorado.
